correctness.rationale: For a finite independent Bernoulli product, the biased Fourier characters form an orthonormal tensor basis. Each kernel K_lambda(x,Y)=sum_S lambda_S chi_S(x)chi_S(Y) is affine in chi_i(x_i)chi_i(Y_i) conditional on other coordinates. The rare-value evaluation yields mean-zero W_rho supported on [-1,rho]; the alternative evaluation yields mean-zero V_rho supported inside this interval, so the secant/chord inequality proves W_rho dominates V_rho for every complex-affine convex Phi. Successive coordinate replacement gives the claimed convex ordering at the all-rare vertex for *every* complex mask lambda_S. Since K(x,y)=K(y,x) algebraically and measure has full support, the sharp L1 and L∞ operator norms equal the same rare-row absolute expectation E|sum_S lambda_S prod_{i∈S}U_i|. A second chord comparison proves monotonicity in alpha_i. The degree<=2 projection follows from the elementary symmetric square identity; fixed alpha>0 CLT+LLN with bounded L2 moments gives limit norm/n=((1−alpha)/alpha)sqrt(2/(pi e)). Independent exact rational tests checked 90 nonnegative/negative signed masks over dimensions 1..5 and all row masses; convexity for every complex Phi follows analytically, not by testing finitely many Phi.
residual_risks: Finite product and positive coordinate biases required; no infinite-product extension, no uniqueness of maximizing row. Fixed-bias asymptotics are not uniform in vanishing alpha.

value.rationale: A common norming vertex for every diagonal Fourier multiplier is an operator-algebraic structural theorem, not a disguised bound for one projector. It replaces maximization over all 2^n evaluation rows by a single explicit product expectation and yields a strong convex ordering/monotonicity principle. These are natural and potentially reusable invariants for biased Fourier truncation and signed filters, beyond the already-known affine and symmetric masks.
residual_risks: An earlier abstract convex-order lemma may make the proof shorter than expected, but importance rests on its all-multiplier consequence; no claims for general non-diagonal projections.
